channel.title: Inbox Signal — Week of 16–23 Nov 2026
channel.description: Linked items from this week's newsletter digest.

item.title: Railway's breach went from a build-system foothold to customers' AI provider keys in three phases
item.description: Railway's postmortem times each phase: monorepo theft took 5 steps in 11 hours, cloud SSH access 4 steps in 10 hours, and AI provider keys 3 steps in 3 hours.

item.title: Agents met 78% of required criteria on average, but only 29% of runs met all of them
item.description: Stripe's integration evals found agents met 78.1% of required criteria on average, and only 29.4% of runs met every required criterion.

item.title: OpenJDK has a 9.2-severity pre-auth RCE in AVX-512 Base64 decoding: patch or disable the intrinsics
item.description: CVE-2026-114938 affects OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later on x86-64 and can enable pre-auth remote code execution in apps such as Jenkins, Confluence and Tomcat.

item.title: Human review of agent-written PRs is dying, so review releases instead
item.description: CodeRabbit's CEO Harjot Gill says he pushed more than 5,000 PRs in a month with agents, and estimates AI spend of about $250K to $275K a month, roughly $150 per PR; that per-PR figure is his own estimate.

item.title: AI-written code still needs owners, and review capacity is the bottleneck because it does not scale
item.description: Freshworks CTO Murali Swaminathan says AI output often duplicates code, sometimes 100 lines where 10 would do.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO raised $81.3B at $83 a share, the largest offering on record [TLDR]
item.description: TLDR reports Anthropic sold about 980 million shares at $83, raising $81.3B at a fully diluted market cap near $1.5T, with trading on Nasdaq as ANT.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO raised $81.3B at $83 a share, the largest offering on record [Big Technology]
item.description: TLDR reports Anthropic sold about 980 million shares at $83, raising $81.3B at a fully diluted market cap near $1.5T, with trading on Nasdaq as ANT.

item.title: A petition to return Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO passes 160,000 signatures
item.description: The petition is reportedly backed by Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney and Garry Tan.

item.title: Nvidia reported $115.8B of quarterly revenue, up 103%, with data-centre revenue of $107.6B
item.description: Per the post, Nvidia's FY2027 Q3 revenue was $115.844B, up 103% year on year, and data-centre revenue reached $107.6B, up 110%.

item.title: The SEC review of Nvidia widened to accounting treatment, and Nvidia closed down 14%
item.description: Per the post, Nvidia closed down 14.01% after the SEC review widened from disclosure to accounting, and Anthropic (ANT) fell 8.5% on its second day of trading.

item.title: Nvidia trades near a 15-year-low multiple of about 11x forward earnings
item.description: Ahead of Q3 results the market expected about $109B of revenue and a 90% earnings increase.

item.title: GPT-6.2 Astra is cheaper per task, but Anthropic still holds the top score [Latent Space]
item.description: Latent Space reports that Artificial Analysis scores Astra 62 on its Intelligence Index, just behind Fable 5.2 at 65, and that Sol matches September's Astra at about 15% of the cost per task.

item.title: GPT-6.2 Astra is cheaper per task, but Anthropic still holds the top score [Artificial Analysis]
item.description: Latent Space reports that Artificial Analysis scores Astra 62 on its Intelligence Index, just behind Fable 5.2 at 65, and that Sol matches September's Astra at about 15% of the cost per task.

item.title: Gemini 4 Carbon took about seven times Astra's steps on bug fixes, and many were off-ticket [Kernel]
item.description: In a private benchmark, Gemini 4 Carbon spent close to an hour on bug fixes that Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra finished in minutes, taking about seven times Astra's steps, half of them unnecessary.

item.title: Gemini 4 Carbon took about seven times Astra's steps on bug fixes, and many were off-ticket [Google]
item.description: In a private benchmark, Gemini 4 Carbon spent close to an hour on bug fixes that Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra finished in minutes, taking about seven times Astra's steps, half of them unnecessary.

item.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen claims 2.5x faster tasks and over fivefold fewer fabricated claims
item.description: Per 9to5Google as summarised by TLDR Design, Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5x faster at its default high setting, more than triples its Terminal-Bench 4.1 score and cuts fabricated claims by over fivefold, with a native 1M-token context.

item.title: Claude Docs launched with 60 server errors across 2 billion requests and no rollback
item.description: The launch ran on about 50 memory-optimised pods and was hardened with a 'chaos loop' before and during launch.

item.title: A Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is out as 1.3GB of Lean, still unverified
item.description: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge announced the claim on 20 November, released as Lean code of about 1.3GB.

item.title: Gartner expects weak AI governance to disrupt 40% of infrastructure and operations organisations by 2028
item.description: Gartner's survey found 95% of respondents reported an agent-related incident in the past year, yet only 15% have automatic circuit breakers to stop runaway agents.

item.title: A clean agent run can still miss its promised output, so check obligations rather than run status
item.description: Citing CarryOn, the author reports that on 168 AppWorld tasks with Claude Sonnet 5, full-history context solved 43.5% of tasks, against 79.8% with a small control state that tracks outstanding obligations plus selected raw evidence.

item.title: Replit's 32 coordinated Opus agents reached an 18.9x NumPy speedup, against 3.7x for one agent
item.description: Replit's optimisation benchmark found the coordinated team reached the speedup in two hours.

item.title: Google's Sashiko reviews Linux patches, and merged commits show 35% fewer 60-day follow-up fixes
item.description: Sashiko separates bug finding from verification using parallel specialist sessions and completes about 1,200 reviews a day after seven months in production.

item.title: Apple is building an agent that controls devices, apps, browsers and code
item.description: Bloomberg reports Apple is hiring for a proactive agentic assistant that writes code, browses and navigates devices, and handles multi-step tasks across apps.

item.title: Google says attackers now deploy autonomous agent frameworks, and California sues OpenAI over agent testing
item.description: Google's Threat Intelligence Group saw attackers using autonomous frameworks such as CAIRN and PentAGI.

item.title: OpenAI says its models cut chip area by about 13% and improve AMD GPU designs by up to 14%
item.description: OpenAI reports its models reduced cell area by about 13% in the vector unit and 10% in the matrix unit of its Jalapeño inference chip.

item.title: More reasoning can make an LLM worse, because a wrong early step gets built upon
item.description: ByteByteGo cites a study where a model asked '2 + 3' reached five, then kept producing until it had written thirteen solutions to the same question.

item.title: Evals for AI engineers: failures come from three separable gulfs, and the fix depends on which one
item.description: The excerpt frames LLM app failures as comprehension, specification and generalisation gulfs, within an analyse-measure-improve loop.

item.title: Agents need a permission ladder, and models should be judged on finished tasks
item.description: Google's Tasks runs each account in a dedicated VM, asks for confirmation before purchases and supports a spending cap.

item.title: Black Forest Labs argues that training on images, video and sound together builds 'visual intelligence'
item.description: BFL trains FLUX 3 on the three signals together, and derives its video upscaler from the same backbone for temporal consistency.

item.title: Claude models appear trained on protein sequences at scale, and frontier agents can spot alignment evals [Blog]
item.description: The author reports the latest Claude models predict next amino acids in little-studied bacterial proteins, which no other tested model could, and fail when sequences are shuffled.

item.title: Claude models appear trained on protein sequences at scale, and frontier agents can spot alignment evals [METR]
item.description: The author reports the latest Claude models predict next amino acids in little-studied bacterial proteins, which no other tested model could, and fail when sequences are shuffled.

item.title: NVIDIA-backed deals reached $219.5B this year, 27.2% of global VC value
item.description: PitchBook figures show seven frontier labs took 80.3% of NVIDIA-linked deal value on 6.4% of deal count.

item.title: An AWS tech lead argues AI adoption must be bottom-up and safe to experiment in
item.description: Patricia Juarez Muñoz's AI learning series at AWS Berlin ran sessions for 15 to 60 people, with managers and individual contributors learning together and volunteers running sessions.

item.title: A spec should take about 10% of implementation time and unblock execution, not replace it
item.description: Jarosław Żołnowski at XTB treats spec-driven development as his most important habit, using a Requirements, Design, Tasks contract that real work must pass through.

item.title: As code gets cheap, verifying AI-written code becomes the hard problem
item.description: In a conversation, Satya Nadella describes 'software factories', with Azure's networking team using agents to run operations across more than 500 fibre network operators.

item.title: Most coordination exists because people left alone make too many wrong calls
item.description: The author splits coordination into sync (a meeting), async (decide, then wait for approval) and none (decide, and revert if wrong), ordered by throughput.

item.title: A small team says AI now delivers because its bots are organised like staff [Tolaria]
item.description: The author describes a chief-of-staff bot for everyone, area-manager and PM bots, and eight collaboration patterns.

item.title: A small team says AI now delivers because its bots are organised like staff [Verity benchmarks]
item.description: The author describes a chief-of-staff bot for everyone, area-manager and PM bots, and eight collaboration patterns.

item.title: Venture returns on YC batches swing about 24-fold, so spread money across batches [Fund returns]
item.description: AngelList's Demo Day funds range from 11.45x net (Winter 2019) to 0.47x (Summer 2016).

item.title: Venture returns on YC batches swing about 24-fold, so spread money across batches [YC index]
item.description: AngelList's Demo Day funds range from 11.45x net (Winter 2019) to 0.47x (Summer 2016).

item.title: Experts cannot easily state what they know, so asking for 'shared context' fails
item.description: Cutler argues that experienced people struggle to explain what they know, what they need and which decisions they are making, even when they are competent.

item.title: Finishing in the top 5 of 100 beats 95% of the field, but chasing an unreachable ideal guarantees dissatisfaction
item.description: The author was a principal engineer at Amazon in the top 1 to 2% of engineers, but never reached distinguished engineer, a level only about 2% of principal and senior principal engineers reach.

item.title: Robinhood's CEO had a rescue term sheet ready before the 2020 crisis
item.description: Vlad Tenev says a term sheet was lined up in March 2020, when volume ran three times the prior month, and it stayed on the shelf after Robinhood raised from Sequoia and D1.

item.title: Plural's €1bn Fund III keeps the rule: pass on anything without a 100X path
item.description: Khaled Helioui says the firm passes on founders whose best projected outcome is $30 to 40bn.

item.title: Exponential View spends about $10,000 a month on AI, and AI-written drafts pull writers off course
item.description: Azhar estimates about 75% of that spend goes on tokens and 25% on subscriptions, and says a retired chart-watermarking tool was replaced by a one-line prompt.

item.title: Engineering output is often the visible bottleneck, not the real one
item.description: Drawing on Ackoff's efficiency-versus-effectiveness distinction and Deming's warning against optimising parts, the author argues that making individuals produce more code does not improve system performance.

item.title: An architect's job is communication: build deliberate views instead of relaying messages
item.description: The argument is that handwaving at complex systems impresses but does not transfer understanding, so architects should cut a system down to the three things that decide the question at hand.

item.title: AI-written code is outrunning CI, so pipelines become the bottleneck
item.description: A freeCodeCamp tutorial linked from TLDR Dev lists five fixes: measure slow steps, cache dependencies, use faster runners, parallelise jobs and tests, and skip redundant work with path filters and cancellation.

item.title: PostHog gates expensive LLM calls with decision models, and 98.7% of session summaries skip the rewrite
item.description: The argument is that many AI features should be cheaper classifiers or scorers that route requests before an LLM runs.

item.title: Audits flagged 134 passing AI patches, but humans confirmed real bugs in 21 of 41 sampled flags
item.description: BenchProofer adds formal specifications and audits to all 500 SWE-Bench Verified tasks.

item.title: Microsoft's agent-framework 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 shipped a credential stealer in a .pth startup hook
item.description: The payload ran whenever Python started, even without importing the package.

item.title: Next.js has had 51 security advisories this year, and 70% sit in code at least a year old
item.description: The Next.js team credits AI tools with finding old bugs.

item.title: Coding agents still reach for dated web patterns, and third-party scripts remain an attack path [Report URI]
item.description: A malicious script, since removed, was injected via an Optimizely A/B testing flaw into pages on Zoom, the BBC and GitLab, according to Report URI.

item.title: Coding agents still reach for dated web patterns, and third-party scripts remain an attack path [Node.js]
item.description: A malicious script, since removed, was injected via an Optimizely A/B testing flaw into pages on Zoom, the BBC and GitLab, according to Report URI.

item.title: The State of HTML 2026 shows declarative features winning, while datalist sentiment falls [State of HTML]
item.description: Details and summary (72.5%) and dialog (67.8%) are the most used interactivity features, and Popover API use reached 40%.

item.title: The State of HTML 2026 shows declarative features winning, while datalist sentiment falls [Chrome]
item.description: Details and summary (72.5%) and dialog (67.8%) are the most used interactivity features, and Popover API use reached 40%.

item.title: Teams are moving from frontier APIs to open models, and the first multi-tenant step runs into latency limits
item.description: The article reports Uber cut per-token costs about 50%, Pinterest 90% and AT&T 56% by moving to open models.

item.title: Solid 2.0 is stable and drops the SolidStart meta-framework
item.description: Server functions move into the core framework, and dev server, SSR and builds now run through Solid's Vite plugin.

item.title: Tailscale puts your devices on a private WireGuard mesh, which suits agents that need private access
item.description: Bytes explains that Tailscale nodes form a WireGuard mesh coordinated by a control plane, with relays when direct connections fail, and positions it as an alternative to ngrok or Cloudflare Tunnels for agents that need databases and MCP servers without public exposure.

item.title: A framework-free RSC walkthrough, local Playwright visual regression, and a React Fiber explainer [RSC]
item.description: The RSC piece (37 min) advises waiting for production adoption, given thin documentation and little ecosystem outside Next.js.

item.title: A framework-free RSC walkthrough, local Playwright visual regression, and a React Fiber explainer [Visual regression]
item.description: The RSC piece (37 min) advises waiting for production adoption, given thin documentation and little ecosystem outside Next.js.

item.title: A model-graded Stop Hook can stop Claude Code saying 'done' while tests are red
item.description: The author asked Claude Code to add idempotency logic to a payment callback and got 'Done, tests pass', but npm test was red because only one test had been run.

item.title: One '@claude' comment on an issue produced a reviewable PR in nine minutes
item.description: The author replied to a tester's 500-on-Save issue with one line asking Claude to find the bug from the repro steps and open a PR.

item.title: Claude Code's /loop can watch a CI run and ping you when it finishes
item.description: The author lost 20 minutes refreshing CI every two minutes, ten times, then used /loop for half a month.

item.title: Claude Code Artifacts turn a debugging session into a web page a colleague can open
item.description: A production debugging session produced more than 200 terminal lines, and three screenshot attempts failed to carry the context.

item.title: Event-driven failures are silent, so consumers must be idempotent and the event design sets the coupling
item.description: The post contrasts Event Notification, where consumers call back for details and so stay coupled at runtime, with Event-Carried State Transfer, where the event carries the state and consumers survive a producer outage.

item.title: Start from the measured bottleneck, and pick the cheapest fix that clears it
item.description: The post introduces twenty decision trees and an escalation ladder: fix the query, cache, scale up, add replicas, partition, specialise, shard, redesign.

item.title: Retries configured at three layers turned a 90-second database failover into sustained overload
item.description: The failover finished at 10:14, but the service was still down at 10:20, with payment request volume at four times baseline.

item.title: Salesforce pairs vertical and horizontal autoscaling on EKS for over $5M in savings
item.description: VPA adjusts CPU and memory while HPA scales replicas on proxy connection count, so the two controllers respond to different signals.

item.title: Concurrency is about program structure, parallelism is about simultaneous execution, and the workload decides
item.description: The guide argues adding threads to an I/O-bound server, or an event loop to a CPU-bound pipeline, can make things slower.

item.title: Classify application state before choosing Redis, Postgres or Kafka
item.description: The guide gives Postgres thousands to low tens of thousands of writes a second on a primary, Redis hundreds of thousands of operations a second per instance, and Kafka hundreds of thousands to millions of records a second.

item.title: Most slow databases come from query patterns, missing indexes or pool settings, not database limits
item.description: Rank queries by total time, calls times average duration: a 5 ms query run 50,000 times a minute costs more than a 3-second report run once a day.

item.title: Standard RAG loses accuracy as collections grow, and GraphRAG answers relationship questions
item.description: The post cites an accuracy drop of up to 12% when the collection grows from 10,000 to 100,000 pages.

item.title: Microservices interview answers are judged on the costs and trade-offs they name
item.description: The 13-question guide covers API gateway, saga, circuit breaker, monolith-first and outbox patterns, and repeatedly argues for stating the failure mode.

item.title: Learn architecture patterns in career order, because each level's pain makes the pattern meaningful
item.description: The post sorts patterns into junior (6), middle (12 more, 18 in total) and senior (11 more, 29 in total) tiers, explaining each by problem, cost and misuse.

item.title: Instacart's LLM query understanding cut tail-query complaints by 50% in A/B tests
item.description: Precomputed tags for head queries mean only about 2% of queries reach the live fine-tuned Llama-3 8B model.

item.title: Stripe's AI Index shows aggregate AI revenue up 103%, but median growth trails well behind [Stripe]
item.description: The index tracks about 20,000 AI businesses paying through Stripe and beats the SaaS Index on aggregate growth, but the gap to median growth suggests the largest AI companies are doing much better than typical ones.

item.title: Stripe's AI Index shows aggregate AI revenue up 103%, but median growth trails well behind [Lovable]
item.description: The index tracks about 20,000 AI businesses paying through Stripe and beats the SaaS Index on aggregate growth, but the gap to median growth suggests the largest AI companies are doing much better than typical ones.

item.title: Non-AI software billing through Stripe grew more than 30% year on year
item.description: Software stocks lost an estimated $2 trillion early this year on fears AI would replace business apps.

item.title: Agents check the cost of every call, so high per-call fees push them to call less or route around you
item.description: SaaStr's own agents cut calls to one vendor by about 90% after that vendor's bill rose 40%.

item.title: 58% of vertical software still prices AI on the seat, and 15% charge on outcomes
item.description: A survey of 126 vertical software founders and operators finds 58% still tie AI pricing to the seat, 15% charge on outcomes, and 28% see no ACV lift.

item.title: The bar is now $1M to $100M ARR in five years, and most SAFEs convert at their cap [SaaStr]
item.description: SaaStr proposes a benchmark of reaching $100M ARR within five years of hitting $1M, because lower public revenue multiples push the required revenue higher at each round.

item.title: The bar is now $1M to $100M ARR in five years, and most SAFEs convert at their cap [Carta]
item.description: SaaStr proposes a benchmark of reaching $100M ARR within five years of hitting $1M, because lower public revenue multiples push the required revenue higher at each round.

item.title: n8n went from a $270M valuation to $5.2B in 14 months, and its founder prizes a dependable process over a demo
item.description: Jan Oberhauser says n8n raised a $1.5M seed in 2020 before any deck, a $180M Series C at $2.5B in October 2025, and SAP bought in at $5.2B in May 2026.

item.title: The AI selloff erased about $8T in 45 days, and the real exposure may be private venture marks
item.description: The S&P 500 closed at 6,910.39, 11.6% below its 6 October record, and Nvidia fell to $125.53 from $239.24; the $8T total is the author's own estimate.

item.title: Salesforce handed its neglected low-score leads to an AI agent that reported over $100M in pipeline
item.description: The piece argues focus beats more outreach.

item.title: 'AI-native' can mean three different things for a product org, so the answer depends on the company
item.description: Bashir lists three facets: product surface, operating model and business strategy.

item.title: Agents act through structured site tools, and Shopify's tests show that is faster than the UI
item.description: In Shopify's tests, agents completed all 60 checkout attempts through WebMCP in an average of 10.3 seconds, against 56 successful attempts averaging 27.4 seconds through conventional browser interaction.

item.title: Enterprise dashboards fail on shared metric definitions more than on visuals
item.description: When departments read the same metric differently, accurate dashboards still become unreliable, so governed definitions and stakeholder involvement help adoption more than layout does.

item.title: Only 30% of professionals report AI gains in QA, while detected accessibility errors per home page rose 10.1%
item.description: Level Access surveyed more than 2,500 professionals and found AI sped up planning, design and development, but only 30% report gains in QA and testing.

item.title: Creatives use AI daily, but only one in four who work faster see any extra income
item.description: Of 1,033 creatives across 103 countries surveyed by Envato, 87% use AI at work and 58% use it daily.

item.title: Use AI to surface the few decisions that block a postponed task
item.description: The author argues decision avoidance keeps tasks stuck, and gives a five-step prompt that splits decisions into a few big ones the user answers and small ones given defaults.

item.title: AI knowledge bases go stale because context is overwritten but records must only be appended
item.description: The author argues the hard part of an AI second brain is keeping it accurate.

item.title: A three-role AI builder team in a Claude Project, with an Evals Agent that challenges unsupported claims
item.description: The setup uses PM, CTO and UX Lead role documents as project knowledge, a collaboration protocol in project instructions, and an Evals Agent that labels each claim as evidenced, pattern or assumption.

item.title: Context, Constraints And Consequences
item.description: Michael Heap: leaders help people choose what to work on by providing context, setting constraints and explaining consequences.

item.title: Bad Ideas That Aren't Bad Anymore
item.description: Devon Estes: gut-feel 'bad ideas' keep turning out to work, so question that intuition more often.

item.title: The Rule Of No Surprises
item.description: Ben Balter: tell people bad news early, and thank people for early warnings, or you get watermelon status updates.

item.title: Design For Understandability
item.description: Jonathan Schuster: use design by contract, class invariants and modularity so systems can be understood one piece at a time.

item.title: Self-Reinforcing Quality / Adopting Verification Pattern
item.description: Will Larson: each pull request generates a verification file describing what the harness checked and what it could not verify.

item.title: No AI Slop: A Manifesto
item.description: A short manifesto on keeping human responsibility for AI-assisted work.

item.title: Shell Tricks That Actually Make Life Easier (And Save Your Sanity)
item.description: Christian Hofstede-Kuhn: portable POSIX shell tricks first, then quality-of-life additions for interactive Bash and Zsh.

item.title: One-Way And Two-Way Doors
item.description: James Stanier: teams that tell reversible from irreversible decisions move faster and avoid layers of sign-off.

item.title: How AI Will Change Engineering Leadership In 2027
item.description: Bjorn Roche: 2026 showed how powerful AI can be; 2027 is when leaders learn when and how to apply it.

item.title: How Can I Recover From Sustained Stress And Avoid Exhaustion?
item.description: Andi Roberts: protect sleep first, then build short breaks and longer restoration into how you work.

item.title: Asking Better Questions
item.description: Michael Heap: 'are we on track?' is frightening because of what the asker does not know, so ask with context.

item.title: The Future Of Software
item.description: Thomas Wolf: software is never finished, source code is no longer secret, and every user becomes the architect of their own tools.

item.title: How I Use AI (Oct 2026)
item.description: Ben Stolovitz: now a research engineer who spends about $3,000 a month on tokens and more time supporting scientists than managing engineers.

item.title: The Watchmaker: Building A Mechanical Watch In A Database
item.description: Trevor Dwyer: a database designed a 34-part watch movement, checked that no parts collided and ran it for a minute, computing every tick in SQL.

item.title: Optimizely's delivery was used to push malicious JavaScript to at least 178 organisations
item.description: Attackers targeted cryptocurrency wallets and payment details.

item.title: AWS Interconnect links AWS and Azure privately, and a Java4Shell flaw can give code execution [AWS]
item.description: AWS Interconnect is now GA and replaces the do-it-yourself networking customers built to connect the two clouds.

item.title: AWS Interconnect links AWS and Azure privately, and a Java4Shell flaw can give code execution [The Register]
item.description: AWS Interconnect is now GA and replaces the do-it-yourself networking customers built to connect the two clouds.

item.title: kagent 1.0 schedules agents as actors on warm worker pools
item.description: Idle actors are suspended to free compute and restored when requests arrive, which addresses pod-per-agent limits.

item.title: The same 40% Black Friday discount sold 45 TidyCal copies and 4 SendFox
item.description: The author attributes the gap to price point and impulse buying: TidyCal at $54 was an impulse buy, while SendFox at $114 was not.

item.title: A 95% success rate can hide total failure for one group of users
item.description: Prasanna Vijayanathan argues a trace shows what happened but not why.

item.title: 27,374 B2B buying prompts show most buyer research happens mid-funnel
item.description: A SaaStr analysis of 27,374 B2B buying prompts finds 57% fall mid-funnel, against 15% at discovery.

item.title: DeepMind's post-AGI report projects effective compute growing at least 10x a year
item.description: The author multiplies hardware at about 1.5x a year, algorithms at 3x to 6x, and investment at 2.5x.

item.title: Big-tech revenue is growing while hiring lags, leaving about 185,000 jobs missing across nine firms
item.description: Dror Poleg attributes the gap to productivity gains built up over years that economic pressure finally forced companies to use.

item.title: Sync work builds trust but depends on everyone being free at once; catch failing changes by watching workarounds
item.description: Seth Godin argues sync work builds energy and trust but wastes time, while async gives focus but can drift into fake urgency.

item.title: Apple wants to learn how people use health AI, with up to 200,000 US participants
item.description: The study could include up to 200,000 US adults aged 21 or older with supported iPhones.

item.title: A 165-million-parameter model trained end to end for about $4,200 of compute
item.description: Quark has about 165 million parameters and used about 1,300 H100-hours.

item.title: Agent recovery is three separate problems: restoring the agent, reversing its system changes and undoing its business effects
item.description: Commvault's recovery tools address the first two.
